research_mode: official Home Office, Police.uk, ONS and MHCLG sources only; outcome cohort and timeliness semantics, force QA, persistent identifiers, archive availability, best-fit geography, population constraints and IoD25 Crime Domain construction; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — outcomes for offences recorded in the reporting period
verified_claims: the linked-cohort method follows offences recorded in a defined reporting period to their eventual outcomes
the proportion resolved increases as investigations mature
long-running offences may receive outcomes outside the year in which they were recorded
limitations: an early linked cohort is incomplete and cannot be treated as a final outcome distribution
cohort age must be preserved when comparing forces or offence types

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — investigations closed in the reporting period
verified_claims: closed-investigation outcomes relate to outcomes recorded in the year regardless of when the crime was recorded
dividing outcomes recorded in a year by crimes recorded in the same year can exceed 100 percent
the annex describes such rates as illustrative rather than true rates
limitations: the numerator and denominator may contain different offence cohorts
these rates are not parcel-level probabilities or clearance probabilities

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — timeliness
verified_claims: timeliness measures elapsed time between offence recording and outcome assignment
the annex says timeliness may be used as an efficiency proxy but is not a firm measure
administrative delay between action and system entry can inflate measured timeliness
limitations: recorded assignment delay is not necessarily operational investigation delay
timeliness cannot be converted to parcel safety

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — data quality considerations
verified_claims: the Home Office receives monthly crime, outcome and transferred-or-cancelled data from forces
Home Office statisticians return anomalies or errors to forces for validation or correction
a pre-publication verification exercise asks every force to confirm the Home Office-held data
limitations: quality assurance reduces risk but does not prove error-free record-level data
the process operates at force and publication level rather than parcel level

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — Home Office Data Hub and Crimsec4 sources
verified_claims: the Home Office Data Hub accepts record-level offence detail
a small number of forces still supply monthly aggregated Crimsec4 returns
Crimsec4 covers notifiable offences, outcomes and transferred-or-cancelled records
limitations: record-level and aggregated returns have different analytical capabilities
source-system type must be retained before force comparisons or record linkage

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — Crimsec4 temporal semantics
verified_claims: Crimsec4 outcomes are recorded in the month the outcome is applied
the corresponding offence may have occurred in a different month or financial year
monthly Crimsec4 outcome data therefore do not correspond directly to offences recorded in that month
limitations: same-month division is not a cohort outcome rate
temporal mismatch must not be silently treated as missing or duplicated data

sources.publisher: Home Office
sources.name: Crime outcomes technical annex — transferred or cancelled records
verified_claims: transferred or cancelled records are split into five documented reasons
the categories include jurisdiction transfer, additional information, duplicate, recording error and qualifying self-defence
the record is counted in the financial year when the transfer or cancellation occurs
limitations: a cancelled record is not a negative crime count
pre-April-2016 comparisons require the annex's combined-category caution

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Outcomes for a specific crime API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns the outcome case history for a specified crime
persistent_id is a 64-character identifier intended to persist across data updates
the API id is not guaranteed to remain stable and is not a police identifier
limitations: the persistent identifier does not reveal an exact incident location
case history is unavailable for Police Service of Northern Ireland records

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Outcomes for a specific crime response fields
verified_claims: each outcome contains an internal category code, human-readable name and outcome month
the response can include a person identifier when available
crime location and street fields remain approximate
limitations: person_id availability is not completeness evidence
outcome category sequences must not be collapsed into the latest outcome without explicit intent

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk archive download contract
verified_claims: archive files are complete snapshots as held at a point in history
Police.uk warns that archives other than the latest month are out of date for current use
MD5 sums are published alongside archives for file verification
limitations: MD5 verifies transfer consistency rather than source truth
historical snapshots remain valid only for explicitly historical analyses

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk availability API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint lists available street-level crime dataset months
each month includes the force identifiers that supplied stop-and-search data
availability must be checked before interpreting an empty force-month response
limitations: availability does not guarantee every record has a mappable location
the stop-and-search force list is not a crime-incidence denominator

sources.publisher: Office for National Statistics
sources.name: Small-area population estimates methodology — best-fit lookups
verified_claims: OA-to-ward and OA-to-constituency lookups use a best-fit method
each OA is represented by a population-weighted centroid calculated from Census 2021 information
the higher geography is assigned according to where that centroid falls
limitations: best fit allocates the whole OA and is not an exact boundary intersection
a centroid relationship must not replace parcel point-in-polygon geometry

sources.publisher: Office for National Statistics
sources.name: Small-area population estimates methodology — exact-fit exception
verified_claims: ONS policy generally builds higher-geography statistics from OA best-fit allocations
National Park census estimates are identified as an exact-fit exception
exact-fit census production cannot automatically be repeated for annual mid-year estimates
limitations: exact fit and best fit are distinct methods with different reproducibility requirements
an exception for National Parks does not validate exact parcel joins elsewhere

sources.publisher: Office for National Statistics
sources.name: Small-area population estimates methodology — constraint hierarchy
verified_claims: LSOA estimates are constrained to MSOA estimates
MSOA estimates are constrained to local-authority estimates
OA estimates are apportioned from their parent LSOA and constrained for consistency
limitations: hierarchical consistency is not independent validation of every small-area estimate
population denominators must retain edition, age-sex basis and boundary vintage

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025 technical report — Crime Domain indicators
verified_claims: the Crime Domain contains eight composite indicators
seven indicators use rates per 1,000 at-risk population
burglary uses a rate per 1,000 at-risk properties
limitations: the domain is an LSOA relative-deprivation measure rather than a parcel crime probability
indicator denominators are not interchangeable

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025 technical report — Crime Domain time windows
verified_claims: the seven recorded-crime indicators use six financial years from 2018/19 to 2023/24
the anti-social-behaviour indicator uses two years, 2022/23 and 2023/24
the indicators are expressed as annual-average rates
limitations: the indicators do not share a single observation window
the domain must not be described as a May 2026 crime snapshot

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025 technical report — theft indicator scope
verified_claims: the theft indicator includes theft and robbery sub-categories except shoplifting
the report describes the LSOA distribution of shoplifting as highly skewed and dependent on the presence of shops
shoplifting was excluded as inconsistent with the conceptual design of the indicator
limitations: Police.uk theft categories cannot be assumed to equal the IoD theft indicator
excluded offences must not be reintroduced through a broad all-theft aggregation

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025 technical report — shrinkage estimation
verified_claims: shrinkage estimation is used where small-area rates have large standard errors
the method borrows strength from larger groupings to reduce chance fluctuation
an LSOA score may move toward either more or less deprivation after shrinkage
limitations: published domain scores are not identical to raw local rates
shrinkage does not create parcel-level evidence

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025 technical report — Crime Domain factor weights
verified_claims: the eight Crime Domain indicators are standardised before combination
factor analysis generated non-uniform indicator weights
the published weights range from 0.074 for burglary to 0.154 for violence without injury
limitations: the domain score is not a simple count or arithmetic average
individual weights must not be treated as causal risk coefficients

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English Indices of Deprivation 2025 technical report — spatial smoothing and enhanced assurance
verified_claims: IoD25 reduced the boundary smoothing parameter from 100 metres to 10 metres
the Crime Domain used raw non-anonymised data from the Home Office Data Hub, the Police.uk repository and bespoke extracts from 39 English forces
LSOA counts were reconciled against Home Office force-level and CSP-level aggregates during major processing phases
limitations: the IoD production method is not equivalent to assigning public anonymised Police.uk points to parcels
the enhanced QA process does not prove the current runtime join has executed
